百分之七十。

sentences.en: It's just, like, everything.
sentences.zh: 简直是……方方面面。

sentences.en: Every standard, every specification, that's the world that Herbert Hoover is trying to make.
sentences.zh: 每一个标准，每一个规格，这就是赫伯特·胡佛试图创造的世界。

sentences.en: So, of all these things, one great challenge was the humble screw.
sentences.zh: 所以在所有这些事物中，一个巨大的挑战就是不起眼的螺丝。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, could you talk about this as a challenge and, you know, what we're dealing with here when it comes to a screw?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能谈谈这作为一个挑战，以及我们在处理螺丝时究竟面临着什么吗？

sentences.en: You have to think of the standardization of the screw as a kind of mega standardization.
sentences.zh: 你必须把螺丝的标准化看作是一种超级标准化。

sentences.en: So, if you're standardizing hospital linens, that's an issue for hospital linen producers.
sentences.zh: 如果你在标准化医院床单，那只是医院床单生产商的问题。

sentences.en: If you're standardizing the screw, that's everyone.
sentences.zh: 如果你在标准化螺丝，那关乎所有人。

sentences.en: Screws are in everything.
sentences.zh: 螺丝无处不在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And even if you're producing an object that doesn't have screws in it, like hospital linens, you're doing it with a machine that requires screws.
sentences.zh: 甚至就算你生产的物品本身没有螺丝，比如医院床单，你也是用需要螺丝的机器来生产的。

sentences.en: Let's zoom in on how the screw works for a second.
sentences.zh: 让我们仔细看看螺丝是如何工作的。

sentences.en: The thing that makes the screw hold two objects together is the screw thread, that raised ridge that's wrapped around the cylinder.
sentences.zh: 让螺丝把两个物体固定在一起的关键是螺纹，也就是缠绕在圆柱体上的凸起脊线。

sentences.en: That thread has a particular angle, which used to be different in different screws.
sentences.zh: 这个螺纹有一个特定的角度，而以前不同的螺丝，角度是不一样的。

sentences.en: The variation is not easily visible to the eye.
sentences.zh: 肉眼很难轻易看出这种差异。

sentences.en: You wouldn't look at a 55-degree screw thread angle and think it looks hugely different from a 60-degree one.
sentences.zh: 你不会看一眼一个55度螺纹角的螺丝，就觉得它和60度的有很大区别。

sentences.en: The difference is everything.
sentences.zh: 但这个差异就是一切。

sentences.en: The difference is absolutely everything.
sentences.zh: 这个差异绝对是一切的关键。

sentences.en: The angle of the screw thread has to match the angle of the groove inside the object it's going into in order for it to work.
sentences.zh: 螺纹的角度必须与它要拧入的物体内部槽的角度相匹配，螺丝才能发挥作用。

sentences.en: And you can't really tell if a screw is going to fit into something until you try it.
sentences.zh: 而且在尝试之前，你很难断定一颗螺丝是否能拧进某个东西里。

sentences.en: And more and more, that was becoming everyone's problem.
sentences.zh: 而且渐渐地，这成了所有人的问题。

sentences.en: Like the scale of this isn't just like people agreeing on a thing who are muckety-mucks and bureaucrats in different states or whatever and coming up with legislation.
sentences.zh: 这种规模不仅仅是不同州的官僚和大人物们对某事达成一致、然后出台立法那么简单。

sentences.en: This is literally every person who makes a machine and every machine that makes a thing has to agree on this.
sentences.zh: 这简直是每一个制造机器的人、以及每一台制造物品的机器都必须就此达成一致。

sentences.en: These are tiny, tiny people like who maybe have one machine in their whole factory.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常渺小的小人物，他们的整个工厂可能只有一台机器。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And then you also think that like basically it's a whole world that has to be reconstituted.
sentences.zh: 而且你还得考虑到，基本上这意味着整个世界都必须被重组。

sentences.en: Like, okay, if you have a machine in your factory that is with a now non-compliant form of screw thread, all those spare parts, you have to buy them anew.
sentences.zh: 比如，好吧，如果你工厂里有一台机器，使用的是现在不合规的螺纹形式，那么所有的备件，你都得重新购买。

sentences.en: So there's this recognition that getting a standardized screw needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 所以大家开始认识到，实现螺丝标准化势在必行。

sentences.en: And at some point they achieve it.
sentences.zh: 最终他们在某个时间点做到了。

sentences.en: When did that happen?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候发生的？

sentences.en: That happens in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 那是在20世纪20年代。

sentences.en: It happens under Hoover.
sentences.zh: 它是在胡佛的领导下完成的。

sentences.en: And it's really hard because it's one thing to get the paving brick manufacturers in a room.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难，因为把铺路砖制造商聚到一个房间里是一回事。

sentences.en: But to deal with a screw thread problem, that's everything.
sentences.zh: 但要解决螺纹问题，那就关乎一切了。

sentences.en: Screws are in everything.
sentences.zh: 螺丝无处不在。

sentences.en: And again, it's one of those really tricky things.
sentences.zh: 而且话说回来，这也是那些非常棘手的事情之一。

sentences.en: Everyone wants there to be a standard.
sentences.zh: 每个人都希望有一个标准。

sentences.en: No one wants to lose out.
sentences.zh: 但谁都不想吃亏。

sentences.en: They don't want it to be someone else's standard.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望采用别人的标准。

sentences.en: So Herbert Hoover works his extraordinary magic.
sentences.zh: 于是赫伯特·胡佛施展了他非凡的魔力。

sentences.en: And in 1924, there is a national screw thread standard.
sentences.zh: 在1924年，全国统一的螺纹标准诞生了。

sentences.en: And Hoover, I just imagine him feeling like the moment of his greatest triumph in this bureaucrat's life.
sentences.zh: 我能想象胡佛当时的感觉，觉得这是他这个官僚生涯中最辉煌的时刻。

sentences.en: He says, now the half-inch nuts screw on to all the half-inch bolts.
sentences.zh: 他说，现在半英寸的螺母可以拧进所有的半英寸螺栓里了。

sentences.en: What a dream.
sentences.zh: 多么美好的梦想。

sentences.en: Utopia is ours.
sentences.zh: 乌托邦属于我们。

sentences.en: Put yourself in Hoover's state of mind here if you could.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，请把自己代入胡佛的心境。

sentences.en: Like, you have a screw with you.
sentences.zh: 比如，你手里拿着一颗螺丝。

sentences.en: Like, what do you see when you see this, if you're Herbert Hoover?
sentences.zh: 如果你是赫伯特·胡佛，当你看到这个时，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So if you're Herbert Hoover, the thing that you're the most locked in on is the screw thread angle.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是赫伯特·胡佛，你最死死盯着不放的就是螺纹角度。

sentences.en: And so the screw thread angle that the United States agrees on is the 60-degree angle.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国最终达成一致的螺纹角度是60度。

sentences.en: That's a huge achievement.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的成就。

sentences.en: But that means, like, every other screw thread no longer works.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着，所有其他螺纹都彻底失效了。

sentences.en: Like, at all.
sentences.zh: 可以说是完全失效。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this consortium sort of agrees.
sentences.zh: 所以这个行业联盟算是达成了一致。

sentences.en: Now, this published standard happens, this consortium.
sentences.zh: 接着，这个发布的标准诞生了，这个联盟也成立了。

sentences.en: People vaguely agree they begin to make their things in this 60-degree threading.
sentences.zh: 人们含糊地达成一致，开始用这种60度的螺纹来制造他们的产品。

sentences.en: You know, this solves the problem of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这解决了美国的问题。

sentences.en: This is a huge achievement in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是一个巨大的成就。

sentences.en: Huge.
sentences.zh: 巨大的成就。

sentences.en: But this is not what happened necessarily in the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着世界其他地方也一定会这么做。

sentences.en: So what's going on in the rest of the world in terms of screw threads and things like this?
sentences.zh: 那么在世界其他地方，关于螺纹以及诸如此类的事情，情况是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: It's exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 完全是一模一样。

sentences.en: But you have to imagine that all of the kind of anarchy that the United States was experiencing locally is actually even worse on a global scale.
sentences.zh: 但你可以想象，美国在本土经历的那种混乱，在全球范围内其实还要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: You know, the early 20th century is a time of rapid-paced technological development.
sentences.zh: 你知道，20世纪初是一个技术飞速发展的时代。

sentences.en: And every year that there's just more stuff being made, it starts to matter more how it's made and whether the objects can speak to each other.
sentences.zh: 随着每年生产的东西越来越多，它们是怎么制造的、以及不同物品之间能否互通，变得越来越重要。

sentences.en: I think language is a really good metaphor here.
sentences.zh: 我觉得语言在这里是一个非常好的比喻。

sentences.en: What you have to imagine is that the United States is producing a growing world of industrial objects that all speak 60 degrees.
sentences.zh: 你必须想象，美国正在生产一个不断扩张的工业品世界，它们说的都是60度的语言。

sentences.en: And then when those objects venture out into the world, they encounter a world of foreign objects that, I mean, it's not even a language that's commensurable.
sentences.zh: 然后当这些物品闯入世界时，它们遇到的是一个异国物品的世界，我的意思是，那甚至都不是一种能够相通的语言。

sentences.en: It's not even a language that's comprehensible.
sentences.zh: 甚至都不是一种能够理解的语言。

sentences.en: They're just like, oh, you speak 55 degrees.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是在说，哦，你讲的是55度。

sentences.en: We will never talk.
sentences.zh: 我们永远无法交流。

sentences.en: There's nothing for us to talk about.
sentences.zh: 我们没有什么可谈的。

sentences.en: I don't know what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我听不懂你在说什么。

sentences.en: We can never have any relationship with each other.
sentences.zh: 我们永远无法建立任何关系。

sentences.en: But then World War II came along and demanded that we have a very real screw-based relationship with the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 但随后第二次世界大战爆发了，它要求我们与世界其他地方建立一种非常现实的、基于螺丝的关系。

sentences.en: So there's this famous moment when FDR is trying to explain why, despite the fact that World War II has not yet hit the Americas,
sentences.zh: 所以有一个著名的时刻，当时富兰克林·罗斯福正试图解释，尽管二战尚未波及美洲大陆，

sentences.en: the United States should actually be deeply interested in this war and, in fact, might need to participate in it, if not fighting, at least by supplying material.
sentences.zh: 为什么美国其实应该对这场战争给予高度关注，甚至可能需要参与其中——即使不直接参战，至少也要提供物资支援。

sentences.en: And so the way he puts it is this.
sentences.zh: 他是这么比喻的。

sentences.en: Suppose my neighbor's home catches fire and I have a length of garden hose.
sentences.zh: 假设我邻居的房子着火了，我有一截花园水管。

sentences.en: If he can take my garden hose and connect it up with his hydrant, I might help him put out his fire.
sentences.zh: 如果他能拿走我的花园水管，接在他的消防栓上，我可能会帮他灭火。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I'm a historian.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我是一名历史学家。

sentences.en: I've seen that line, like, many, many times.
sentences.zh: 这句话我见过很多很多次。

sentences.en: And it's always about being a good neighbor.
sentences.zh: 它讲的总是如何做一个好邻居。

sentences.en: But then when you think about it, you're like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 但仔细想想，你会觉得，等一下。

sentences.en: You don't imagine yourself as Herbert Hoover.
sentences.zh: 你不会把自己想象成赫伯特·胡佛。

sentences.en: And you just imagine yourself, like, kind of raising your hand in the back of the room and being like,
sentences.zh: 你会把自己想象成那种在房间后排举手的人，然后说：

sentences.en: whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: What if your hose doesn't fit his hydrant?
sentences.zh: 要是你的水管插不上他的消防栓怎么办？

sentences.en: You've got a serious problem.
sentences.zh: 那你可就有大麻烦了。

sentences.en: And the cost of noncompliant screw threads, it's bad enough during peace.
sentences.zh: 不合规螺纹的代价，在和平时期已经够糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's horror during war.
sentences.zh: 在战争时期简直就是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: In the 1940s, as the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪40年代，随着美国

sentences.en: got more and more involved in the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 越来越深地卷入第二次世界大战，

sentences.en: it quickly became clear this was a different kind of war than we had ever fought before.
sentences.zh: 很快人们就发现，这是一场与以往截然不同的战争。

sentences.en: So World War I was fought with horses.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战是用马匹打的。

sentences.en: World War II is a much more mechanized war.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战是一场高度机械化的战争。

sentences.en: In fact, one of the main ways in which the United States participates in World War II
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国参与二战的主要方式之一，

sentences.en: is essentially acting as quartermaster to the world, as supplying stuff to all of its allies.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是充当世界的后勤总管，为所有盟友提供物资。

sentences.en: It outsources the fighting to other countries, and it just, you know, sends its factories into overdrive.
sentences.zh: 它把战斗外包给其他国家，而自己则开足马力开动工厂。

sentences.en: The problem that everyone recognizes at the start of the war is that none of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 大家在战争初期意识到的问题是，美国的各种装备

sentences.en: stuff plays with the foreign stuff.
sentences.zh: 和外国的装备根本无法兼容。

sentences.en: So there's a Canadian official who just says, look, you have to understand that at the start of the war,
sentences.zh: 所以有一位加拿大官员曾直言不讳地说，你看，你必须明白，在战争初期，

sentences.en: there is not a single gun or a single round of ammunition that can be shared among the allies.
sentences.zh: 没有哪怕一支枪或一发子弹是可以在盟友之间共享的。

sentences.en: The bullets are slightly different sizes.
sentences.zh: 子弹的尺寸略有不同。

sentences.en: And so one bullet doesn't fit another gun.
sentences.zh: 所以一种子弹塞不进另一种枪里。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国的

sentences.en: bombs do not fit the U.K.
sentences.zh: 炸弹不适用于英国的

sentences.en: bomb racks.
sentences.zh: 炸弹架。

sentences.en: And that sounds like a small thing, but like, try dropping a bomb if the bomb doesn't fit on the bomb rack.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是个小问题，但如果你尝试一下就会发现——如果炸弹根本挂不上炸弹架，你怎么把它投下去？

sentences.en: You drop it with your hands.
sentences.zh: 你得用手把它扔下去。

sentences.en: Yeah, you'll drop it, but not in the way you want it to.
sentences.zh: 对，你确实能把它扔下去，但绝对不是你想的那种方式。

sentences.en: And of course, there's a huge problem with the screws.
sentences.zh: 当然，螺丝也带来了巨大的问题。

sentences.en: They're in the weapons, tanks, and planes, which all have to work in faraway places.
sentences.zh: 它们存在于武器、坦克和飞机中，而这些装备都必须在遥远的地方正常运转。

sentences.en: So like, think about sending a Jeep.
sentences.zh: 所以，想想运送一辆吉普车。

sentences.en: So that's a thing that happened a lot.
sentences.zh: 这在当时经常发生。

sentences.en: The United States was sending Jeeps all over the world.
sentences.zh: 美国正把吉普车运往世界各地。

sentences.en: And first of all, it's inefficient to ship a Jeep.
sentences.zh: 首先，整车海运吉普车效率低下。

sentences.en: So what you want to do is you want to do the IKEA method, and you want to ship parts of a Jeep.
sentences.zh: 所以你想用的方法是宜家模式，也就是把吉普车的零件拆散运过去。

sentences.en: But that means you have to have people on the other ends who can put the Jeep together.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着你必须在目的地有人能够把吉普车组装起来。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这没问题。

sentences.en: But then, you know, the Jeep's of course going to break, and it's going to break down in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 但接下来，你知道吉普车肯定会坏，而且会以各种各样的方式抛锚。

sentences.en: So that means you have to have, on the other part of the world, people who know how to work with that Jeep,
sentences.zh: 这意味着你必须在世界的另一端，拥有懂得如何修理这种吉普车的人，

sentences.en: and they have all of the parts that allow them to repair the Jeep.
sentences.zh: 并且他们要备齐所有能够修理吉普车的零件。

sentences.en: And you need that in dozens of countries all at the same time.
sentences.zh: 而且你需要同时在几十个国家做到这一点。

sentences.en: The design, construction, and repair of everything that the Army had to have to survive the war
sentences.zh: 军队为在战争中生存下来所需的一切物资的设计、制造和维修，

sentences.en: all relied on screws that often just didn't fit.
sentences.zh: 全都依赖于那些往往根本装不上的螺丝。

sentences.en: Throughout the war, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在整个战争期间，美国

sentences.en: spent $600 million shipping extra screws, nuts, and bolts overseas
sentences.zh: 花费了6亿美元向海外运送额外的螺丝、螺母和螺栓，

sentences.en: to deal with the incompatibility issues.
sentences.zh: 来应对不兼容的问题。

sentences.en: $600 million on screws.
sentences.zh: 光是螺丝就花了6亿美元。

sentences.en: That's enough money to build 1,000 B-29 bombers.
sentences.zh: 这笔钱足够建造1,000架B-29轰炸机了。

sentences.en: So in the middle of this war, there's a meeting to try to solve some of this problem,
sentences.zh: 所以在战争正酣之际，有一场会议试图解决部分问题，

sentences.en: because the British recognize that they need to sort of get onto the standard.
sentences.zh: 因为英国人意识到他们需要回归统一的标准。

sentences.en: Could you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, first of all, it's amazing in some ways that in the middle of the war,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，首先，在某种程度上这很神奇，在战争期间，

sentences.en: while the British are literally being bombed, they're debating about screw-thread standards.
sentences.zh: 当英国正遭受实实在在的轰炸时，他们却在争论螺纹标准。

sentences.en: But of course they're debating about screw-thread standards, because if you don't work this out,
sentences.zh: 但他们当然得争论螺纹标准，因为如果你不把这事搞定，

sentences.en: the whole thing comes grinding to a halt.
sentences.zh: 一切都会陷入彻底的瘫痪。

sentences.en: Like, Herbert Hoover's point that incompatibility of standards is a massive inefficiency.
sentences.zh: 就像赫伯特·胡佛的观点所说，标准不兼容是一种巨大的效率低下。

sentences.en: I mean, that just sounds like a dorky thing to say, but it turns out if you're in the middle of a war,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来这像是个书呆子气的话题，但事实证明，如果你身处战争之中，

sentences.en: inefficiencies are lethal.
sentences.zh: 效率低下是致命的。

sentences.en: And so you really do want to resolve the screw-thread issue.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实很想解决螺纹问题。

sentences.en: Now, Britain operates on a 55-degree screw-thread, so they don't speak to each other.
sentences.zh: 现在，英国采用的是55度螺纹，所以双方根本无法沟通。
